# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three numbers, and the sources agree on the basics.

| Check | What to look for | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Continuous output** | At least 300-400 W | A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, and older units up to ~350 W ([BlackBox](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). |
| **Surge rating** | At least 1,300 W, and 2,400 W for large or older fridges | The compressor's startup spike is what trips undersized units. Estimates range from 900-1,200 W ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)) to 1,200-2,400 W (BlackBox). Check your fridge's manual if you can. |
| **Capacity (Wh)** | See below | The compressor cycles on and off, so average draw is much lower than running watts. |

Also choose a **pure sine wave** inverter, which all the models below have.

## Capacity by outage length

An efficient 18 cu ft fridge averages about 41 W, which works out to roughly 1,400 Wh per day after inverter losses and 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Other sources assume 50-70 W averages, so check your fridge's EnergyGuide label (kWh per year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts).

- **About 12-17 hours:** ~1,000 Wh
- **A full 24 hours:** ~1,400-2,000 Wh
- **2 days:** ~2,800 Wh or more

Keeping the door shut stretches these numbers. A warm kitchen, an ice maker, or frequent door openings shrink them.

## Picks that fit

- **Budget, about half a day:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W output, and a 2,700 W peak. It's $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF as of Oct 27 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-discount-codes)). It's a good fit for a smaller fridge or a shorter outage.
- **A full day or more:** [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) has 2,073 Wh and was estimated at about 33 hours of fridge runtime ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). It's $899, or $854.05 with the same code.
- **Another 2 kWh option:** The Anker SOLIX S2000 has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W output, and 3,000 W peak ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)). I didn't have a direct purchase link for it.

The Dealectric links are affiliate links, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. The code was tested in BLUETTI's cart, but checkout has the final word on price.

## Quick advice

If you only want to cover a typical overnight or daytime outage, about 1,000 Wh is enough. For a full day with some margin, or if your fridge is large or old, go to about 2,000 Wh. Beware of compact units under about 1,300 W of surge, which often can't start a compressor at all.
